evidence: Quint. 1.5.47: per tempora, ut in verbō … peccātur
terms.comment: The word for time is the word for tense. The question is Cujus temporis est?, what tense is it? (Traupman 241); in the present tense, tempore praesentī (227).

phrases.latin: in participiō per genus et cāsum, ut in vocābulō, per tempora, ut in verbō, per numerum, ut in utrōque, peccātur
phrases.english: in the participle one goes wrong in gender and case, as in a noun, in tense, as in a verb, and in number, as in both
What tense is it? — The present.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 226, p. 227, p. 241, p. 249.
Quintilian checked against the Perseus Latin texts, and cited by its numbering.
